internal.title: Incident Report: Elevated Error Rate in Checkout Service Due to Payment Service Error Injection
internal.body:
At 11:52 UTC on 2026-11-08, an alert was triggered for a high error rate in the checkout service. The investigation identified that the root cause was an error injection in the payment service, specifically the paymentFailure flag set to 50%, which caused invalid token errors during card charging attempts. This led to knock-on errors in the checkout service.

The timeline of the incident is as follows:
- 11:52 UTC: Alert received for high error rate in checkout.
- 12:11 UTC: Diagnosis confirmed payment service error injection as the cause.
- 12:12 UTC: Proposed disabling the paymentFailure flag.
- 12:12 UTC: Approval obtained and flag disabled.
- 12:12 UTC: Recovery verified with error rates returning to normal.

The incident was resolved by disabling the paymentFailure flag, which immediately restored normal service operation. Secondary hypotheses involving resource exhaustion in the ad service and configuration errors in checkout were investigated but not supported by evidence.

Severity: SEV2

Please review the postmortem for detailed analysis and lessons learned.

external.title: Some checkouts failed due to payment processing errors
external.body: Between 11:52 and 12:12 UTC on 2026-11-08, some customers experienced issues completing checkout due to errors in the payment processing system. The issue was identified and resolved by disabling a feature that was causing payment failures. Normal service has been restored, and customers should no longer experience checkout problems.

output.impact: Customers experienced failures completing checkout due to payment processing errors between 11:52 and 12:12 UTC.
output.root_cause: An error injection flag (paymentFailure) in the payment service caused invalid token errors during card charging, resulting in checkout service errors.
output.resolution: The paymentFailure error injection flag was disabled, restoring normal payment processing and checkout service operation.

lessons.lesson: Avoid enabling error injection flags in production environments without thorough impact assessment and monitoring, as they can cause cascading failures in dependent services.
lessons.applies_when: When error injection flags are enabled in the payment service affecting checkout.

action_items: Review and improve the process for enabling error injection flags to include stricter approval and impact analysis.
Enhance monitoring to detect cascading failures from dependent services more rapidly.
